text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Fiat Auto Poland will soon start production of Fiat 126 cars furnished with catalytic converters and stop making the older, environment-unfriendly model, the company said.

- The Nisko-based Nimet mechanical engineering plant will separate from the Warsaw-based Ursus tractor maker and act as an independent firm. In the future Nimet will invite a strategic investor, the plant director Jozef Kielb said.

- Property rights of the formerly state-owned Delecta food concentrate company were passed over to the employee-owned Delecta joint stock company which leased the Wloclawek-based plant two years ago and repaid all liabilities by a deadline.
- The Polish corporate sector's financial condition in the third quarter of 1996 was worse than in the same period last year as costs grew faster than revenues, reducing profitability.
- Poland's food prices edged up by 0.3 percent in October compared with the previous month, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The listed Mostostal Zabrze construction firm will carry out welding works in Germany worth 1.2 milllion marks.
- The net profit of the Polish-American Amplico life insurance firm in the first nine month of 1996 was 7.47 million zlotys, the company president Georges Dourte said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Centrum Daewoo's president Kim Woo-Choong has confirmed the Korean parent company's plans to invest around $2 billion in Poland's motor industry, electronics makers and real estate.
- The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has approved the Rafamet machine tool maker's listing on the over-the-counter (OTC) market.
- Solidarity trade unions at the Bialystok-based furniture maker BFM have demanded an all-employee monthly salary rise of 110 zlotys and the current president's dismissal.
- The Dutch Makro Cash and Carry wholesale and retail chain invested $200 million in Poland in the last two years.
GAZETA WYBORACZA
- Peugeot Poland plans to sell 7,000 cars this year, a 65 percent growth compared with last year, the company said.
- Around 30 firms from Poland, Switzerland, Germany and Japan are exhibitding at the construction machinery international fair in Opole, southwestern Poland.
- France's Hachette Filipacchi Presse has acquired the remaining 50 percent stake in the Elle Poland women's magazine publisher and now owns it fully.
ZYCIE

- A consortium of the Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej (BWR) regional development bank, PKO SA bank and Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH) bank will manage an issue Krakow municipal bonds worth 15 million zlotys to finance modernisation of the city's public transport system.
PARKIET
- Poland's KPW has greenlighted public share trading of Kruszwica oil maker and Grajewo chipboard plant and of the listed Farmfood food maker's new share issue.
- "I'm fully satisfied with the regulation of Poland's capital market which is now mature and safe for the Pioneer Trust Fund investments", the Pioneer trust vice-president Larry Wilder said.
